etymologies.etymologyHTML:
Borrowed from Middle French blond m, from Old French blond, blont, blund, (> Medieval Latin blondus), from Frankish *blund (“a mixed color between golden and light-brown”), from Proto-Germanic *blundaz (“mixed, blinding”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰlendʰ- (“to become turbid, see badly, go blind”). Compare Old English blondenfeax (“grey-haired”), Old English blandan (“to mix”). More at blend.

Alternative etymology connects Frankish *blund to Proto-Germanic *blundaz (“blond”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰl̥ndʰ-, *bʰlendʰ- (“blond, red-haired”). If so, then it would be cognate with Sanskrit ब्रध्न (bradhná, “ruddy, pale red, yellowish”).

definitions.definition: Of a bleached or pale golden (light yellowish) colour.

quote.citation: 1914, “American Anthropologist”, in (Please provide the book title or journal name):
quote.text: She has a blond complexion, with brown hair and gray eyes.

quote.citation: 2011 Feb, “Beauty Confessions”, in Redbook, volume 216, number 2, page 60:
quote.text: If you're going one or two shades lighter, don't even touch your brows. But if you're making a big change, soften them by tinting them with home haircolor: a lighter shade of brown for blonder shades, a golden shade if you're dyeing your hair red.

quote.citation: 1956, James Baldwin, chapter 2, in Giovanni's Room, Penguin, published 2001, Part 2:
quote.text: He seemed—somehow—younger than I had ever been, and blonder and more beautiful, and he wore his masculinity as unequivocally as he wore his skin.

quote.citation: 2012 Jan, “The Best Blonde Hair Color in Hollywood”, in Cosmopolitan‎[1]:
quote.text: Blonde bombshells have been around since the beginning of time, but lately, stars have really been stepping up their golden-haired game.

quote.citation: 2010, Mariah Stewart, Moon Dance, Simon & Schuster, →ISBN:
quote.text: “She was so blond, that where it said 'sign here,' she wrote Gemini.” He had given her only the weakest of smiles.

quote.citation: 2002, Michael Jay, The Altherian Code, iUniverse, →ISBN, page 118:
quote.text: Katelyn's laugh was nearly uncontrollable. “You are so blond sometimes,” she said with a long laughing sigh, but then calmed herself down.

definitions.definition: A pale yellowish (golden brown) color, especially said of hair color.
A person with this hair color.
